notes: Release x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; Linux 6.8.0-147-generic. No owned build or test overlaps measured load.
Two 60-second points per fresh daemon/socket placement: requested 8 million frames/s per direction, then unlimited. Processes and sockets persist between points.
64-byte Ethernet frames have one VLAN and 18 UDP payload bytes; 128-byte Ethernet frames have two VLANs and 78 UDP payload bytes.
Reported Gbit/s counts UDP payload only. Frames/s is delivered payload rate divided by UDP payload length. Goodput excludes drain; loss and drop counters include drain.
Single-tag ordinary UDP uses reader-local lanes; QinQ uses strict flow hashing. Socket and TAP queue placement may differ between independently started runs.
Repeating the retained single-tag binary restores near-baseline goodput with more even worker utilization. Initial low throughput is observed but is not isolated as a storage-code regression.
QinQ reverse goodput still falls under unlimited load. These observations do not establish a CPU ceiling or pass the acceptance gates.
Source queue, socket overflow and TAP drops count SKBs and can each affect many frames; do not add them into an exact frame-loss total.
